chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about what is lawful for a man from a menstruating woman. He said: “Nothing, until she becomes pure.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Its meaning is that nothing is lawful for him of intercourse in the vagina, even though what is besides that is lawful for him, as the earlier reports have contained. Then he said—may Allah the Exalted support him—the minimum days of menstruation are three days, its maximum is ten, and its average is what lies between that. This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ: days, referring here to the duration of menstruation

ai.seo_question: What is permissible between spouses during menstruation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning intimacy with a menstruating woman and states that intercourse is not permitted until she becomes pure. The compiler then clarifies that the prohibition refers specifically to vaginal intercourse, and he also notes the juristic limits of menstruation as a minimum of three days and a maximum of ten days.
